methods.name: DC-Merge
methods.full_name: DC-Merge: directional-consistency model merging (energy smoothing + cover-space merging)
methods.paper_title: DC-Merge: Improving Model Merging with Directional Consistency
methods.formula_latex: \Delta_i\approx U_i\Sigma_iV_i^{\top}\ \ (\text{rank-}r\text{ SVD of the task vector }\Delta_i=W_i-W_0\text{ or }\Delta_i=B_iA_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}},\ i=1,\dots,T);\ \ \bar\Delta_i=U_i\bar\Sigma_iV_i^{\top},\ \ \bar\Sigma_i=\Big(\tfrac1r\textstyle\sum_{j=1}^{r}\sigma_i^{j}\Big)I_r\ \text{(averaging) or }\bar{\boldsymbol\sigma}_i=\Big(\textstyle\sum_{j}\sigma_i^{j}\Big)\mathbf w,\ \mathbf w\text{ linearly decreasing},\ \textstyle\sum_j w_j=1,\ \tfrac{w_1}{w_r}=\min\!\big(\tfrac{\sigma_i^{\max}}{\sigma_i^{\min}},\rho\big)\ \text{(linear smoothing)};\ \ U=[U_1,\dots,U_T]=PSQ^{\top}\ \Rightarrow\ \widetilde U=PQ^{\top}=U(U^{\top}U)^{-1/2}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times k},\ \ \widetilde V\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times k}\text{ likewise from }[V_1,\dots,V_T],\ \ k=rT;\ \ M_i=\widetilde U^{\top}\bar\Delta_i\widetilde V\in\mathbb{R}^{k\times k};\ \ \widetilde M=\mathrm{Merge}(M_1,\dots,M_T)\ (\text{TA or TIES, entry-wise});\ \ \Delta\widetilde W=\widetilde U\big(\widetilde M\odot\mathcal M\big)\widetilde V^{\top},\ \ \mathcal M=\mathrm{blockdiag}(\mathbf 1_{r\times r},\dots,\mathbf 1_{r\times r});\ \ W=W_0+\alpha\,\Delta\widetilde W;\ \ \text{frozen: }W_0\text{ and all task vectors; nothing is trained (}\alpha\text{ is picked on validation data)}

methods.locus: Every 2-D weight matrix of T task-adapted copies of one base model: CLIP ViT-B/32, ViT-B/16 and ViT-L/14 visual encoders, either fully fine-tuned (8/14/20 tasks) or LoRA-tuned on the q, k, v and output projections at r = 16 (8/12/16 tasks), and LLaVA-v1.5-7B LoRA checkpoints (MM-MergeBench, 8 seen tasks plus 4 unseen). In the released code, non-matrix parameters are simply averaged.
methods.structure: Training-free, layer-wise merge of \(T\) task matrices in three steps. (1) Energy smoothing: each task vector is truncated to rank \(r\) and its singular values are flattened (to their mean, or to a linear profile whose max/min ratio is at most \(\rho\)), while its singular directions \(U_i,V_i\) are kept. (2) Cover space: the column-concatenated bases \(U=[U_1,\dots,U_T]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times rT}\) and \(V\) are replaced by their polar (whitened) factors \(\widetilde U=PQ^{\top}\), \(\widetilde V\). These are the orthonormal matrices nearest to \(U\) and \(V\), the same orthogonalisation TSV-M uses. The paper motivates them as a near-optimal solution of a shared-dyadic-basis reconstruction problem (its Eqs. 7-8, 23-25). (3) Every smoothed task vector is written in the cover coordinates as a \(k\times k\) matrix \(M_i=\widetilde U^{\top}\bar\Delta_i\widetilde V\) (\(k=rT\le\min(d_{out},d_{in})\)). These matrices are combined entry-wise by TA or TIES (the released full-fine-tuning code uses TIES after keeping the top 0.1% of each \(M_i\)). Only the \(T\) diagonal \(r\times r\) blocks are kept before mapping back, which gives one dense delta of rank at most \(rT\) per matrix. Because \(\mathrm{span}(\widetilde U)=\mathrm{span}(U)\supseteq\mathrm{col}(\bar\Delta_i)\), the round trip \(\widetilde U M_i\widetilde V^{\top}=\bar\Delta_i\) is exact. With TA and no mask, the cover-space step therefore reduces to summing the smoothed task vectors. Its effect comes from the block-diagonal mask, which drops cross-task coordinates, and from coordinate-wise rules such as TIES applied in the cover basis. This follows from the construction and is consistent with the paper's ablations (Tables 5-6), but the paper does not state it. Diagnostic metric: \(\mathrm{DirSim}(\Delta_s,\Delta_t)=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{nm}}\mathbf 1_n^{\top}R(s,t)\mathbf 1_m\) with \(R_{ij}=(u_s^{i\top}u_t^{j})(v_t^{j\top}v_s^{i})\). This is cosine similarity with every singular value set equal, and its projected version correlates with post-merge per-task accuracy (Pearson \(R=0.64\)).
methods.mergeable_reason: The output is one static delta per matrix, \(W=W_0+\alpha\,\widetilde U(\widetilde M\odot\mathcal M)\widetilde V^{\top}\), folded into the base weights. The result is a single model with no adapters, routing or inference overhead. Merging LoRA inputs gives a dense rank-\(\le rT\) delta, not a rank-\(r\) LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free). \(\alpha=0\) recovers \(W_0\). For \(T=1\) with TA, \(\widetilde U=U_1\), \(\widetilde V=V_1\) and \(M_1=\bar\Sigma_1\), so the method returns the energy-smoothed rank-\(r\) version \(U_1\bar\Sigma_1V_1^{\top}\) of the task vector, not the task vector itself.
methods.key_idea: How much of each task survives merging depends on keeping the singular directions of its task vector, not the energy in its singular values. The paper measures this with an energy-blind directional similarity. DC-Merge therefore flattens each task's spectrum and then merges all tasks in one shared orthonormal cover basis \((\widetilde U,\widetilde V)\), keeping only the diagonal \(r\times r\) blocks so that each task's directions survive aggregation.
methods.results_note: On LoRA-tuned (r = 16) CLIP ViT-B/32, DC-Merge reaches 64.17/68.40/66.27% average absolute accuracy for 8/12/16 merged tasks, against 63.01/66.28/64.61% for the strongest baseline Iso-CTS, and it is best in 7 of the 9 full-fine-tuning settings.

relations.note: Cited and used as a baseline. The cover basis is TSV-M's orthogonalisation of the concatenated per-task singular vectors (\(U_\perp=PQ^{\top}\)). TSV-M places each \(\Sigma_i\) in its own diagonal block. DC-Merge first smooths each spectrum, projects every smoothed task vector into the shared basis, merges with TA/TIES and keeps the diagonal blocks, so cross-task contributions inside each block are retained.

Strongest baseline (Iso-C/Iso-CTS, Marczak et al., ICML 2025, arXiv 2502.04959; not in the catalogue). Iso-C flattens the spectrum of the merged matrix, over a common plus task-specific subspace in Iso-CTS. DC-Merge instead flattens each task's spectrum before merging and then aligns tasks in a cover basis.
TIES (or TA) is the rule applied entry-wise to the cover-space coefficient matrices \(M_i\). TIES applied in cover coordinates does better than TIES applied to raw weights (Table 6).
Task vectors and the final \(W_0+\alpha\,\Delta\widetilde W\) follow Task Arithmetic, and TA is one of the two in-cover-space aggregators.
LoRA-merging baseline (KnOTS-TIES). KnOTS also aligns tasks in a shared SVD basis before applying TIES. DC-Merge beats it in all nine reported LoRA settings and on KnOTS's own released checkpoints.

Not cited. Core Space also maps each task's LoRA into a shared \(Tr\times Tr\) coordinate matrix, merges there with an off-the-shelf rule and maps back. Its bases come from SVDs of the stacked LoRA factors. DC-Merge uses whitened per-task singular bases, spectral smoothing and a block-diagonal mask.

methods.name: MaLoRA / MaRA
methods.full_name: MaLoRA: Mamba-modulated Low-Rank Adaptation, with the MaRA Mamba Retrieval Adapter
methods.paper_title: Selective State-Space Adaptation and Retrieval for Language Model Reasoning
methods.formula_latex: h_t=W_0x_t+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\,\lambda_t\,BAx_t,\ \ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r};\ \ \lambda_t=\operatorname{softplus}\big(w_\phi^{\top}o_t+b_\phi\big)\in\mathbb{R}_{>0};\ \ (o_1,\dots,o_t)=\mathrm{Mamba}\big(Px_1,\dots,Px_t\big),\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \ s_t=\bar A_t s_{t-1}+\bar B_t u_t,\ o_t=C_t s_t\ (\bar A_t,\bar B_t,C_t\text{ computed from the current input; one Mamba-1 block of width }r,\ d_s=16);\ \ \text{i.e. }\Delta W_t=\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\,\lambda(x_{1:t})\,BA;\ \ \text{frozen: }W_0;\ \text{trained jointly: }A,B,P,\text{ the Mamba block},w_\phi,b_\phi;\ B_0=0,\ b_\phi\approx\operatorname{softplus}^{-1}(1);\ \ \text{MaRA (separate stage, LM frozen): }H_i=\mathrm{LM}_{1:K}(Q\Vert C_i),\ p_i=\textstyle\sum_j\operatorname{softmax}_j\big(q_a^{\top}\tanh(W_kH_{i,j})\big)H_{i,j},\ (s_1,\dots,s_N)=\mathrm{Mamba}(W_{in}p_1,\dots,W_{in}p_N),\ r_i=\mathbf w_\ell^{\top}s_i,\ \text{keep the top-}k\text{ segments}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ (\text{LoRA})+r\,d_{in}\ (P)+6r^2+6r\,d_s+4r\lceil r/16\rceil+16r\ (\text{Mamba-1 block of width }r,\text{ expand }2,\text{ conv }4,\text{ plus scalar head})\ \text{per adapted matrix}\ (\approx3.4\text{k beyond }P\text{ at }r=d_s=16);\ \approx+56\%\text{ over LoRA in total }(47.9\text{M vs }30.7\text{M, mean over Qwen-2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Gemma-2-9B});\ \text{MaRA: }\approx2.9\text{–}3.1\text{M per model}
methods.locus: q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, up_proj and down_proj of every decoder layer of Qwen-2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B (also Qwen-2.5-3B). Each projection in each layer has its own modulator, which reads that projection's input \(x_t\) and runs causally over the token sequence. MaRA reads the hidden states of the first \(K\) frozen layers (\(K=12\) to \(20\)) for each (query, paragraph) pair and acts on the context before generation.
methods.structure: A rank-\(r\) LoRA delta whose magnitude is a positive scalar gate that depends on the token history, \(\Delta W_t=\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\lambda(x_{1:t})BA\): the direction \(BA\) is static and only the strength changes per token. The gate is a causal, stateful function of the prefix: a selective state-space (Mamba/S6) recurrence of width \(r\) over the projected inputs \(Px_1,\dots,Px_t\), read out by a linear head and a softplus. It can therefore both suppress (\(\lambda<1\)) and amplify (\(\lambda>1\)) the update. The TopLoRA baseline instead inserts a stateless per-token diagonal \(\Lambda(x_t)=\mathrm{diag}(\exp(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Px_t)))\). MaLoRA trades the diagonal for a scalar (a stateful diagonal variant gave no consistent gain, Appendix C) and gives the gate memory across tokens. READ and SSMLoRA also use recurrence, but across layers; MaLoRA's runs across tokens. At the token level, GRU and LSTM gates perform about the same as the Mamba gate, so recurrence itself is what matters there. The paper notes that with KV caching the recurrence is restarted at each generated position, so only the prompt is modulated with its full history. MaRA is a separate adapter at the retrieval level, not a weight update. It combines an attention pool over frozen early-layer states, a two-layer Mamba that runs over paragraphs rather than tokens, and linear local and global scoring heads. It selects the top-\(k\) paragraphs over \(N_p=4\) chained passes and is trained on supporting-paragraph labels against the unadapted backbone, separately from MaLoRA.
methods.mergeable_reason: The effective delta \(\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\lambda(x_{1:t})BA\) changes from token to token, so it cannot be folded into \(W_0\). The modulator must run at inference: one \(d_{in}\to r\) projection plus a width-\(r\), \(d_s=16\) Mamba step per token. Folding is possible only if \(\lambda\) is frozen to a constant \(c\), giving \(W_0+c\,\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\), and that changes the model.
methods.identity_at_init: \(B_0=0\) gives \(\Delta W_t=0\) and \(h_t=W_0x_t\) for every token. In the released code the gate bias starts at \(\operatorname{softplus}^{-1}(1)\approx0.54\) (plus small noise) and the readout weights are small, so \(\lambda_t\approx1\) and training starts as plain LoRA. The paper notes that its Eq. 3 reduces to LoRA when \(\lambda\equiv1\).
methods.key_idea: LoRA applies one static update to every token. MaLoRA rescales that update per token with a gate \(\lambda(x_{1:t})\) produced by a Mamba recurrence over the prefix, so the adapter's strength depends on the whole trajectory up to token \(t\), not only on \(x_t\). The learned gate is mostly suppressive and separates token roles (markers and query versus content), but it does not separate supporting from distractor paragraphs. That limit motivates MaRA, which applies the same state-space idea one level up as a paragraph selector of about 3M parameters.
methods.results_note: At r = 16, MaLoRA alone raises MuSiQue F1 over LoRA from 51.1/54.4/59.8 to 56.4/62.3/63.7 on Qwen-2.5-7B/Llama-3.1-8B/Gemma-2-9B (ahead of stateless TopLoRA in every cell), and adding MaRA gives +6.4 F1 over LoRA on average across the 3x2 backbone-dataset grid.

relations.note: Setting \(\lambda_t\equiv1\) recovers LoRA (the paper's Eq. 3 reduces to Eq. 1).

TopLoRA (Li et al., NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2510.23123; not in the catalogue) is the direct stateless predecessor and main baseline. It places a per-token diagonal \(\exp(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Px_t))\) between \(A\) and \(B\). MaLoRA keeps the projection \(P\) but replaces the stateless diagonal with a stateful scalar from a Mamba recurrence.

Cited (SSMLoRA, NAACL 2025, arXiv 2502.04958; not in the catalogue). SSMLoRA uses a state-space model to link LoRA modules of the same type across layers. MaLoRA's recurrence runs across the tokens of one input inside each projection.
Cited (READ: Recurrent Adaptation of Large Transformers, arXiv 2305.15348; not in the catalogue). READ propagates a recurrent state through the adapter stack across layers, not across tokens.

Not cited. aLoRA also makes the LoRA contribution depend on token position, through a hard causal switch that turns on at the invocation token. MaLoRA learns a soft, content-dependent causal gate that is active on prompt tokens too, so it gives up aLoRA's reuse of the base model's KV cache.
Static baseline in Tables 4 and 6. DoRA trains 1.90x slower than LoRA, MaLoRA 1.16x slower.
Static baseline in Tables 4 and 6 (+50% parameters over LoRA, versus +56% for MaLoRA).

notes: Batch 5 of the 2026 sweep, pass 2. Of the three requested methods, two are kept (DC-Merge and MaLoRA/MaRA) and one is skipped (CoRA). None duplicates a catalogued id; checked against existing_index.json and every methods list in raw/ and verified/. SKIPPED, not a PEFT method: CoRA (Correlation-aware Adapter, arXiv 2603.21828; ICLR 2026 poster, verified via the OpenReview search API, forum JRlNrcTllN, public since 2025-10-08). (a) The TSFM backbone is not frozen. Section 3 defines the adapter as fine-tuning the base model F into F*, and every result compares 'fine-tuning with CoRA' against 'fine-tuning without CoRA' under the same backbone recipe. In the released code (github.com/decisionintelligence/CoRA), freeze_backbone() is commented out, and the plugin-stage optimizer is built over the backbone's parameters (optim.Adam(self.model.fm.parameters())). For Timer and similar backbones nothing is frozen. Section 6.5 counts CoRA's parameters only as an addition on top of the backbone. Its 'lightweight' claim concerns O(N) inference complexity, not trainable-parameter savings. (b) The low-rank time-varying/time-invariant correlation estimate R+Q_tVQ_t^T (polynomial Q_t) is used only during training, to set the positive/negative pairs of the contrastive loss. At inference CoRA is an output-side residual head: per-channel MLP blocks with an SE-style softmax channel weight, a linear forecasting head, and a per-channel convex gate beta with the backbone's own forecast. So CoRA is an auxiliary head plus contrastive regulariser for ordinary TSFM fine-tuning, not a parameter-efficient method. If the catalogue wants it anyway, it belongs as a fine-tuning add-on with year 2025 (OpenReview first public). VENUES: DC-Merge is in CVF open access for CVPR 2026 (and OpenReview LZacqcAohT). It is unrelated to the rejected ICLR 2026 submission 'From Coefficients to Directions' (MDA, different authors). MaLoRA/MaRA is EMNLP 2026 main per its arXiv comment and repo README; the EMNLP 2026 accepted list was not checked. Years follow first public versions: DC-Merge arXiv v1 2026-03-06; MaLoRA arXiv v1 2026-07-21. IDS: 'malora-mamba' avoids a clash with MALoRA (Mixture of Asymmetric LoRA, arXiv 2410.22782, 2024). The entry covers MaLoRA as the PEFT update and describes MaRA, a retrieval adapter, inside it. NEW RELATION TARGETS not in the catalogue: iso-cts (arXiv 2502.04959, ICML 2025), toplora (arXiv 2510.23123, NeurIPS 2025), ssmlora (arXiv 2502.04958, NAACL 2025) and read-recurrent-adapter (arXiv 2305.15348). DERIVED, NOT STATED: (1) MaLoRA's per-matrix parameter formula comes from the released code: a mambapy MambaBlock with d_model=r, expand 2, d_conv 4, d_state 16, dt_rank=ceil(r/16), plus an r->1 readout and an r-vector gate bias. Summed over Qwen-2.5-7B's q,k,v,up,down it gives +56.8% over LoRA, matching the paper's ~56%. (2) DC-Merge's polar-factor cover basis spans exactly the concatenated task subspaces, so with TA and no mask the cover-space round trip is the identity and reduces to summing the smoothed task vectors. The gains in the paper's Tables 5-6 therefore come from the block-diagonal mask and from TIES applied in cover coordinates. The paper writes Eq. (5) of CoRA's correlation as R+Q_tVQ_t^T with V=sigmoid(ReLU(E_1E_2^T)). The code instead uses (R+sigmoid(Q_tV_1V_2^TQ_t^T))/2; this matters only for the skipped entry.
